Subject: MAP draft + cost checklist — tokens/$ assumptions

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. I've attached our current MAP worksheet (Novus_MAP_v2.xlsx). Procurement wants a short cost gating checklist we can use in the mutual action plan: specifically we need clear acceptance criteria around tokens-per-dollar, cache hit assumptions, and any batching tradeoffs that would affect tail latency.

A few specifics from our side:
- Expected steady-state queries: ~12k/day, with one peak window (US East) that can spike to 3x for a few hours (simulated 36k/hr).
- We have conversational flows averaging ~420 tokens in (prompt + context) and we assume ~60 tokens out.
- Procurement target: predictable unit economics and documented risks for spikes.

Can your team provide a short checklist (numbers + configuration knobs) we can insert into the MAP and a short recommended canary timeline? We want the MAP to include gating that prevents rollout to prod unless a small canary demonstrates cost and latency targets.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if helpful.

— Alice

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the MAP draft and the traffic details — very helpful. I sketched a focused gating checklist and a short canary plan below. I'm copying Ben for sim numbers and Jordan for timeline/ops.

Key assumptions (please confirm):
- Avg request size: 480 tokens total (you noted ~420 in + ~60 out).
- Baseline cache hit: conservative 25% prefix/KV hit for initial pilot; we can improve with prefetching.
- Typical concurrency during steady-state: 40 qps; burst up to 120 qps for short windows.

Quick unit-econ sensitivity (rough):
- No-cache, conservative batching (max_batch_size=8, max_wait_ms=20): ~tokens/$ = $0.0032 per avg request.
- Prefetch + warmed KV (estimated 60% hit) + batching (max_batch_size=16): ~tokens/$ = $0.0019 per avg request.
- Aggressive batching (max_batch_size=64) lowers tokens/$ further but increases 95th-tail latency; not recommended for live clinical flows.

Suggested MAP gating checklist (numbers are our recommended acceptance thresholds for canary):
1) Unit cost: per-request tokens/$ <= $0.0022 (measured over 48 hours of canary traffic mirrors).
2) Cache hit: observed prefix/KV hit-rate >= 50% during canary (prefetch enabled).
3) Tail latency: 95th percentile inference latency <= 350 ms (end-to-end from request to token-stream start).
4) Burst resilience: under 3x traffic spike, 99th-percentile latency degradation <= 2x baseline and no sustained request failures.
5) Logging & traces: token-level cost traces + example prompt set recorded for regression checks.

Operational knobs we propose to lock in for the canary (we'll run these in the Canary policy):
- batching: max_batch_size=32, max_wait_ms=50
- prefetch: enabled, prefetch window=30m TTL, prefetch concurrency limited to avoid traffic amplification
- KV cache: retention 1M tokens per model shard, fallback model variant in config for low-capacity zones

If those thresholds look reasonable I can have Ben run a 48-hour simulated traffic run and produce a short sim CSV you can attach to the MAP. Also propose a simple canary timeline: 7 days of controlled traffic ramp (3k/day -> 12k/day -> 36k/hour short spike) followed by decision window. Jordan — can you confirm that timeline aligns with your suggested ops dates?

Happy to tighten any numbers if Novus has stricter cost targets.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP draft + cost checklist — tokens/$ assumptions

Thanks — ran the sim against the MAP traffic profiles Grace shared. Attaching the sim summary but calling out the highlights here. Note: these are simulation outputs using our canary config (see bottom).

Sim scenarios (48-hour windows):
- Baseline (no prefetch, conservative batching): observed tokens/$ ~ $0.00325 per avg request; cache hit ~22%; 95th latency ~290 ms under steady-state.
- Prefetch-warmed KV (prefetch window 30m, TTL 30m), batching (max_batch_size=16): tokens/$ ~ $0.00195; cache hit ~63%; 95th latency ~340 ms under steady-state; during 3x short spike 95th ~420 ms but <500ms and no request failures.
- Aggressive batching (max_batch_size=64, max_wait_ms=100): tokens/$ ~ $0.00115 but 95th latency jumps >800 ms — unacceptable for interactive flows.

My recommendation: adopt the Prefetch-warmed config for canary and require the unit-cost gate at tokens/$ <= $0.0022 (gives buffer from sim median). Also require that observed cache hit >= 50% and 95th latency <= 350 ms. If the canary meets the gates we can phase to GA with the same defaults and monitor for 2 weeks post-GA.

Canary config we used (included in sim-summary.csv):
- model variant: rwd-large-3b-quant
- batching: max_batch_size=32 (preferred), max_wait_ms=50
- prefetch: enabled, prefetch concurrency cap=12, TTL=30m
- cache eviction: LRU per shard, retention target ~1M tokens
- fallback: rwd-small-compat in low-capacity zones

I'll attach sim-summary.csv (CSV with per-hour tokens/$ and latency buckets). Grace — if you want I can also produce a short one-page memo that maps these sim rows to the MAP gating language for procurement.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
